STRIPE CHURN AND COHORT ANALYZER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Where do your Stripe subscribers actually leave?

Drop in the CSV you exported from Stripe and get your MRR waterfall, monthly churn, a cohort retention table and plain-language findings, without connecting an analytics vendor to your billing account or sending anyone your customer list.

The file is read in this browser tab and never leaves your device. Customer IDs and emails in it are not sent anywhere.

1. Your subscriptions export

Stripe Dashboard → Billing → Subscriptions → Export (all columns). Needs a start or created date and an amount; canceled or ended dates, interval, quantity, customer and plan columns are used when present. Other tools' exports work if the headers are similar.

Choose a file or paste CSV text, then click Analyze.

Result

MRR waterfall by month

MonthStart MRRNewChurnedEnd MRRCustomersLogo churn

Cohort retention (share of each start month still subscribed)

Rows are the month a subscription started. Columns are months since. Green is retained; a cell is blank until that month has happened.

What would a price rise do?

Uses the active subscriptions and each plan's own recent churn from your file. The two sliders are your assumptions, not predictions: nobody can know how many customers a rise will lose until it happens.

What is lower churn worth?

Projects MRR 12 months out at your recent churn and recent new MRR, then again with churn lower. The slider is your assumption, not a prediction.

The model, and what it leaves out

  • MRR per subscription is the export's amount normalised to a month (yearly ÷ 12, weekly × 52/12) times quantity when present, held constant for the subscription's life.
  • Waterfall. Start MRR + new − churned = end MRR every month. A subscription that starts and ends in the same month counts in both, so the table always reconciles.
  • Logo churn is subscriptions ended in a month divided by subscriptions active at its start; the summary uses the last three complete months.
  • Lifetime is 1 ÷ monthly logo churn and revenue LTV is average revenue per subscription × lifetime. It is revenue, not profit, and is unreliable when churn is near zero.
  • Price-rise simulator. Takes the subscriptions active now on one plan, applies your rise, removes the share you say cancels at once, then decays the rest at that plan's own recent monthly churn (plus any lift you add) for 12 months, and compares with no rise. Break-even is the cancelled share at which the two totals are equal. It is arithmetic on your assumptions, not a forecast; it ignores grandfathering, annual contracts that renew later, and customers who downgrade instead of leaving.
  • Not modelled: upgrades and downgrades, coupons, tax, refunds, failed-payment recovery, usage billing. A customer who cancels and resubscribes shows as one churn and one new subscription.

Common questions

Can I get churn and cohort retention out of Stripe without a paid analytics tool?

Yes. Export your subscriptions from the Stripe Dashboard (Billing, Subscriptions, Export) as CSV and drop it here. The tool computes MRR, new and churned MRR, monthly churn and a cohort retention table from the start and cancel dates in the file. Nothing is uploaded; the file is read in your browser.

How is MRR calculated from the export?

Each subscription's amount is normalised to a monthly figure (yearly divided by 12, weekly times 52/12) and multiplied by quantity if the file has a quantity column. Each subscription's MRR is held constant at that value, because a subscription export has no history of upgrades, downgrades or discounts.

What does the tool not see?

Expansion and contraction between plans, coupons, tax, refunds, failed payments and usage billing. A customer who cancels and resubscribes appears as one churn and one new subscription. Treat the numbers as an estimate from the dates and amounts in your file.

What is the difference between logo churn and revenue churn?

Logo churn is the share of customers who left in a month; revenue churn is the share of MRR they represented. If small plans leave more than large ones, revenue churn is the lower of the two.

Is this financial advice?

No. It applies arithmetic to the file you provide and does not replace your own records or a qualified adviser.

Prefer a terminal or a monthly cron job? Use the command-line version. Weighing this against a connected analytics product? Read the comparison.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional. Results are estimates that depend entirely on the file you provide. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it, and for any business decision you make. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your file is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (csv_analyzed, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Also running a subscription business? See the Stripe failed payment recovery analyzer, MRR waterfall calculator, the SaaS annual plan discount calculator the subscription price impact calculator and, for shops without subscriptions, the customer lifetime value predictor.

Keeping your own books? The Stripe payout to journal converter turns a payout report into month-split Xero or QuickBooks journals, checked against the payout.

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

vs-chartmogul-baremetrics.html.text:
← Stripe Churn and Cohort Analyzer

This analyzer vs. ChartMogul and Baremetrics for Stripe churn

Connected subscription-analytics products read your billing account and keep a dashboard current. If all you need is MRR, churn and cohort retention from the subscriptions you have, a Stripe CSV export and a local analysis answers it for free, with no account and no read access handed to anyone. Here is where each approach fits.

Side by side

QuestionConnected analytics productThis CSV analyzer
SetupConnect your Stripe account (read access to billing data) and wait for the importExport a CSV from the Stripe Dashboard, drop it in the page or run node cli.mjs
Where your data goesTo the vendor, under its terms and security practicesNowhere. Read in your browser tab or local process; the page makes no network requests with your file
CostCheck each vendor's current pricing pageFree, MIT licensed
MRR, new and churned MRR, logo and revenue churnYesYes, from start and cancel dates and amounts
Cohort retention by start monthYesYes
Expansion and contraction MRR (upgrades, downgrades)Yes, from invoice and event historyNo. Each subscription's MRR is held constant
Discounts, refunds, trials, failed-payment recoveryTypically yesNo. A subscription export does not carry them
Always-current dashboard, alerts, team accessYesNo. You re-export when you want a fresh reading
Price-rise what-if with break-even cancellation shareVaries by productYes, built in, labelled as assumptions rather than a forecast
Scriptable alert when churn passes a limitVaries by productYes: --max-churn exits 1 in a cron or CI job

The right-hand column describes this tool exactly. The middle column describes the general category from the vendors' public descriptions; check a product's own documentation for what it supports today.

When a CSV is enough, and when it is not

A CSV is enough when you are an early-stage founder checking whether churn is concentrated in the first months, comparing plans, sizing a price rise, or preparing a board or investor note once a month and you would rather not give a third party billing access to do it.

Use a connected product when expansion revenue is a large part of your story (seat-based or usage-based pricing), when discounts and refunds distort your real revenue, when several people need a live dashboard, or when you want failed-payment recovery and alerts without lifting a finger. Those need history a subscriptions export does not contain.

Do it in three steps

  1. In the Stripe Dashboard open Billing → Subscriptions and export as CSV.
  2. Drop the file into the analyzer, or run it from a terminal: 
    node cli.mjs subscriptions.csv --cohorts
node cli.mjs subscriptions.csv --max-churn 5   # exit 1 if monthly logo churn > 5%
  3. Read the findings first (early-life churn, rising churn, concentration, plan gaps), then the cohort table.

Export labels in the Stripe Dashboard change over time. The analyzer recognises the common header names and lists any row it cannot read with a line number and reason.

Questions

Is there a free alternative to ChartMogul or Baremetrics for Stripe churn?

For a one-off or monthly look at MRR, churn and cohort retention, yes: export your subscriptions from the Stripe Dashboard as CSV and analyze the file in your browser or with the command-line version. Nothing is uploaded and no account or API key is needed. It reads start and cancel dates and amounts, so it cannot see upgrades, discounts, refunds or failed payments the way a connected product that reads your full billing history can.

What do connected analytics tools do that a CSV analysis cannot?

Products that connect to your billing account can read invoice and event history, so they can report expansion and contraction MRR, discounts, refunds, trials and failed-payment recovery, keep the dashboard current without a monthly export, and join billing data with other sources. A subscriptions export carries only the dates and amounts on each subscription, so this tool holds each subscription's MRR constant and shows new and churned MRR only.

Can I run it automatically every month?

Yes. The command-line version reads a CSV from a file or stdin and can exit with status 1 when monthly logo churn passes a threshold you choose, so a cron job or CI step can flag a spike. You still need to export the CSV from Stripe; it does not connect to your account.

Are these tools affiliated with this one?

No. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by ChartMogul, Baremetrics, Paddle or Stripe. Their names are used only to describe what each kind of tool does.

Free, open source (MIT). Estimates from the dates and amounts in your file; not legal, tax, or financial advice. No warranty. Sponsor.
